content: Retroactive/backfilled verification evidence is treated as a weaker evidence class than contemporaneous system-generated records. The named failure mode is assembling proof after the fact from institutional memory rather than from artifacts that show the control operated over time; the standard mitigations are (a) derive evidence from immutable system output, not from summaries of the work, and (b) hash-link records so retroactive modification is detectable. Backfilling under deadline pressure is also associated with scope compression: the retroactive pass silently redefines the criterion to whatever the shipped artifact happens to satisfy.
